protein: LbCas12a (Cas12a/Cpf1, type V-A CRISPR RNA-guided endonuclease)
assay_method: nanoDSF (differential scanning fluorimetry, intrinsic Trp fluorescence). Prometheus NT.48 (NanoTemper); 0.5 mg/ml protein in 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 500 mM NaCl; 20-95 degC at 1 degC/min.
remark: Activity at 50 degC is reported for only WT and 5 variants, so it is not included.

protein: T7 RNA polymerase (single-subunit DNA-dependent RNA polymerase)
assay_method: Thermal shift assay / DSF with SYPRO Orange (5x). Analytik Jena qTower3; ~0.2 mg/ml protein, 20 ul, in triplicate; 25-65 degC in 0.5 degC steps with 5 s hold; Tm from a Boltzmann fit of the unfolding curve.
remark: P657L is excluded: no expression, no Tm. Activity at 52 degC is reported for only WT and 5 variants, so it is not included.

assay_method: Thermal shift assay / DSF with SYPRO Orange (5x). Analytik Jena qTower3; 0.3 mg/ml protein in 1x PBS; 25-85 degC in 0.5 degC steps with 5 s hold; Tm from a Boltzmann fit of the unfolding curve.

protein: VHH (camelid single-domain antibody against growth hormone), with C-terminal DDDDK-SGGGGS-His6 tag
readout: EC50(untreated) / EC50(24 h in 0.3 M NaOH), fold retained
assay_method: Indirect ELISA against plate-bound growth hormone (5 ng/well); VHH incubated in 0.3 M NaOH for 24 h and neutralized with HCl, then serial dilutions 1:2 to 1:2048, HRP secondary, TMB, A450; EC50 from a four-parameter log(agonist)-response fit.
remark: Readout is EC50(untreated)/EC50(treated), computed from the two EC50 columns the source reports separately, so that higher is better.

protein: Phi29 DNA polymerase (highly processive strand-displacing B-family DNA polymerase with 3'-5' proofreading exonuclease)
assay_method: Differential scanning fluorimetry (DSF) with SYPRO Orange (Protein Thermal Shift Dye Kit, Thermo Fisher). Roche LightCycler 480 II; 19 ul of 0.1 mg/ml protein in 25 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.4, 500 mM NaCl plus 1 ul diluted dye; 25-99 degC at 0.05 degC/s; Tm from Protein Thermal Shift software.
remark: Supplementary Table 1 prints two rounds of top-20 predictions (ESM-1v zero-shot, and ESM-1v after FSFP training) as two side-by-side ranked blocks; they are merged into one dataset here. T441L, G245V, V130L and C290K appear in both blocks with identical Tm values and are kept once. Sequence is the native 575-aa polymerase (UniProt P03680), which mutation numbering verifies against; the pET28a N-terminal His-tag of the assayed construct is not included, as its sequence is not given.

readout: Expression fitness score: log2 of the variant's weighted-mean yeast surface-display signal over that of wild-type DAOx; higher means more correctly folded enzyme displayed
assay_method: Yeast surface display in S. cerevisiae EBY100 (pYDKan, a pYD1 derivative in which the Aga2 linker is replaced by GTPTPTPTPTGEF). Displayed DAOx was detected by fluorescent labelling and cells were sorted by FACS into four bins of increasing display signal; variant abundance per bin was read out by Illumina UMI sequencing on a NovaSeq 6000 and converted to cell numbers, and the expression score was taken as the expected fluorescence across the four bins (weighted mean). Two biological replicates, Pearson r = 0.94 (n = 7069).
remark: The sequence is UniProt P80324, which every one of the 364 scanned positions verifies against with no offset; the assayed molecule was the Aga2 display fusion carrying an N-terminal GTPTPTPTPTGEF linker and a C-terminal tag, and only the enzyme itself is given here. The scan covers positions 2-365, so positions 1 and 366-368 carry no variant. 333 nonsense variants were dropped as a premature stop cannot be written as a substitution, as were the 512 rows of Fig2_I whose score cell was empty. The 363 synonymous rows all read exactly 0 and are the wild-type protein, so they are represented by the single WT row rather than kept separately. The wild type reads exactly 0 because the score is defined as a log2 ratio against it, not because it was measured separately. Not extracted: the twelve individually cloned variants used to validate the screen, below the 20-variant floor, and the FoldX delta-delta-G values, which are computed rather than measured. Two sources were merged for this readout: Fig2_I, the heat-map sheet, and FigS6_A, which supplies expression scores for 19 position-365 variants that Fig2_I leaves blank; the 6380 variants present in both agree to floating-point precision (largest difference 1e-15).

protein: NST-M1 (sulfotransferase domain of heparan sulfate N-deacetylase/N-sulfotransferase 1, PROSS-designed variant NST-design3)
readout: Residual N-sulfotransferase activity (IU/L) after 30 min at 50 degC, assayed at 37 degC
assay_method: Variants of the NST sulfotransferase domain were expressed from pGEX-4T-1 in E. coli Origami B (DE3) with 0.2 mM IPTG. Enzyme was incubated at 50 degC for 0.5 h and the residual activity then measured at 37 degC; one IU is the transfer of 1 umol of sulfate from donor to acceptor per hour. The assay was run on microtiter plates with pNPS as sulfo donor, aryl sulfotransferase IV, and deacetylated heparin pentasaccharide as acceptor, following 405 nm absorbance from p-nitrophenol release. Three independent samples per variant.
remark: The reference is not the wild type: NST-M1 is the PROSS design NST-design3, which carries 15 substitutions relative to wild-type NST (G625S, S637P, E660D, V699I, D721N, S738D, S741P, K743E, A767Y, K779Q, E784D, T807H, E839P, L842E, T869P); its sequence is quoted from Supplementary Table 2 and equals UniProt P52848 residues 558-882 with those changes applied. The paper describes the construct as residues L557-R882, but the sequence it prints begins one residue later, at L558. Mutations are named in full-length P52848 numbering while this file is 1-indexed against the 325-residue fragment, so every position was shifted down by 557; all 37 genotypes verify against the parent after that shift, and none of them touches a position already changed in NST-M1. The wild-type row is the NST-M1 control measured on the same plates. The readout is a heat-challenge survival measure rather than plain turnover, which is why this sits under thermal stability even though its unit is an activity. Two rounds were merged, the 21 single mutants of Fig. 3D and the 16 combination mutants of Fig. 3E, which share the readout and the parent. Rows dropped: five single mutants of Fig. 3D whose mean cell is empty in the source (N705A, D843E, A846R, Y864K, K698I) and two combination rows likewise empty, plus the rows prefixed M2-, M4- and M6-, whose values differ from the identically named unprefixed rows (274.8 against 201.6, and 340.6 against 194.4) and which therefore sit on a further-accumulated background this file cannot reconstruct. Not extracted: the wild type and four PROSS designs of Fig. 3B, below the 20-variant floor, and the 251 screening readings of Supplementary Data 2, which carry no genotype at all.

protein: ASPA, aspartoacylase (cytosolic; hydrolyses N-acetyl-L-aspartate; loss of function causes Canavan disease), assayed as an ASPA-GFP fusion
source_organism: Homo sapiens (UniProt P45381), expressed in HEK293T
readout: VAMP-seq abundance score, 1 = wild-type-like cellular abundance, 0 = strongly reduced
assay_method: VAMP-seq in a HEK293T landing-pad line. A site-saturated, barcoded cDNA library of ASPA fused to GFP was integrated as a single copy by Bxb1-catalysed recombination at the landing-pad locus; the promoterless plasmid also expresses mCherry from an IRES downstream of ASPA as a per-cell expression control, and non-recombinant cells were removed with AP1903 (rimiducid) via the landing pad's iCasp9. Cells were sorted by FACS into bins on the GFP:mCherry ratio and each variant's frequency per bin read out by barcode sequencing. A protein stability index PSI_i = sum_g(g * f_i,g)/sum_g(f_i,g) was computed per biological and FACS replicate from the bin frequencies f_i,g, then normalised as abundance score = (PSI_i - PSI_stop)/(PSI_WT - PSI_stop), where PSI_WT is the wild-type PSI and PSI_stop the median PSI of stop substitutions, both averaged over replicates. The scale therefore runs from 1 (wild-type-like abundance) to 0 (strongly reduced abundance) by construction.
remark: Readout is the abundance_score column of Source Data sheet "All Variant Data", used as it stands. Sequence is UniProt P45381 (human ASPA, 313 aa) fetched whole; the label check passes with bad = 0 across all 313 positions and all 5947 designed missense labels. The file holds missense substitutions only: the 313 nonsense variants of the same screen cannot be written as {WT}{pos}{MUT} against a protein sequence, and the 313 synonymous variants carry no score in this table. The wild-type row is written as 1.0, which is what the normalisation in the Methods defines rather than a measured value, and is stated as such in the paper. Phase 7: the paper states that "50 out of 61 pathogenic variants displayed an abundance score lower than 0.5" and that there are "11 highly abundant pathogenic variants (abundance score > 0.5)"; taking the ClinVar column of the same sheet, 63 missense variants are annotated pathogenic, 61 of them carry an abundance score, and this file splits them exactly 50 below 0.5 and 11 above. Coverage reconciles with the paper: 5843 missense scores here plus the 308 nonsense scores of the same sheet plus the wild type gives the 6152 of 6260 the abstract reports. Not included as separate work items: the toxicity screen of the same library, which is a separate measurement and is curated as its own dataset under Toxicity/ExpressionToxicity; the 106-tile degron screen of Fig. 5, whose units are 24-residue tiles rather than variants of ASPA; the low-throughput abundance validations (the low_troughtput_abundance_score column, 27 variants); and the RNA-seq differential expression of the same workbook, which is not a per-variant measurement. The gemme_de, normalized_rosetta_ddg, wcn_sidechains_AF, degrons, QCDPred and AF_confidence columns are predictions, not measurements, and the Clinvar and gnomAD columns are annotations.

protein: PLpro, the papain-like protease domain of SARS-CoV-2 nsp3 (viral polyprotein processing, plus de-ubiquitylating and de-ISGylating activity)
source_organism: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (UniProt P0DTD1 residues 1564-1878), expressed in HEK293T biosensor cells
readout: Normalized abundance fitness score from an mClover3 reporter; 1 = synonymous wild-type, 0 = nonsense
assay_method: Barcoded lentiviral single-site mutagenesis library of PLpro under a TetOn promoter, transduced into HEK293T cells carrying a FRET cleavage biosensor; PLpro expression induced with doxycycline and cells sorted by FACS. Barcodes from the sorted gates were sequenced on Illumina and ratiometric per-variant scores with modelled errors computed with DiMSum. Scores were normalised so that the mean of synonymous wild-type variants is 1 and nonsense variants 0, and filtered for low counts and high errors. For abundance, PLpro was expressed as an mClover3 fusion and cells sorted on high versus low mClover3; mRNA was recovered from the sorted gates to count variants. The paper reports about 97% coverage of the 6301 possible single-site variants.
remark: Sequence is the 315-residue PLpro domain derived from the scan itself, per Phase 3f: the WT_AA column of Source Data sheet "Fig. 3" gives a single unambiguous residue at each of positions 1-315, so bad is empty by construction. The derived string is byte-identical to residues 1564-1878 of UniProt P0DTD1 (SARS-CoV-2 pp1ab), which is the canonical PLpro domain, so the check is not circular. The wild-type row is written as 1.0, the value the normalisation defines rather than a measured number. Position 0 of the source tables is the expression construct's initiator Met, outside the paper's own 1-315 numbering, and its 1 missense entry is excluded; nonsense variants and the 570 synonymous controls (which carry no position) are the normalisation anchors, not work items. Phase 7: the paper states that "no mutations were permitted at the PLpro active site (Cys111, His272, Asp286)" and that the four zinc-coordinating cysteines are likewise intolerant. In the activity file all 19 substitutions at each of those seven positions sit near 0 against a wild-type anchor of 1 - position means 0.151 (C111), 0.011 (H272), 0.027 (D286), 0.074 (C189), 0.097 (C192), 0.076 (C224), 0.045 (C226) - against a whole-library mean of 0.612, and the single best substitution anywhere among them reaches only 0.33. The other readouts of the same workbook are separate work items: activity (Fig. 2), abundance (Supplementary Fig. 4), 3k drug escape (Supplementary Fig. 6) and 5c drug escape (Supplementary Fig. 7). The combined 3k-and-5c map (Supplementary Fig. 9, identical to the fitness_drug and fitness_3K columns of sheet "Fig. 4", which agree to 0.0) is a merge of the two per-drug scans and is not shipped separately. Not included: the leaky-expression profile (Supplementary Fig. 11), which measures how poorly a variant's doxycycline control holds rather than a property of the protein; and the recombinant-enzyme kinetics and dose-response curves of Figs. 1, 4 and 5, which cover a handful of variants.

protein: RV3 F, the fusion glycoprotein F0 of human respirovirus 3 (parainfluenza virus 3); assayed as the F ectodomain fused to a GCN4 trimerization domain and a C-tag
source_organism: Human respirovirus 3, JS strain (UniProt A0A059QA82), expressed in cultured cells
readout: Initial BLI binding rate V0 (nm/s) of culture supernatant to immobilized PIA174, a prefusion-specific antibody; higher means more prefusion-conformation F protein
assay_method: Single or double amino acid substitutions were introduced into a plasmid encoding the RV3 F ectodomain fused to the helical GCN4 trimerization domain in register with the heptad repeat of the C-terminal stem, followed by a C-tag (RV3F-GCN4). Three days after transfection, culture supernatants were tested for binding to immobilized PIA174 by BioLayer Interferometry, and the initial slope V0 at the start of the association phase taken as the readout. Values are the mean of the two or three replicate measurements the source data reports for each variant.
remark: Readout is the mean of the replicate columns of Source Data sheet "Fig 1B", taken as they stand; the wild-type row is the measured RV3 F-GCN4 control of the same panel. The 54 variants fall into the paper's three design categories - 19 prolines, 14 disulfides and 21 packing/polar substitutions - and the disulfides and two of the packing designs are double substitutions, written multi-site with a colon. Sequence is UniProt A0A059QA82, the 539-residue human respirovirus 3 fusion glycoprotein F0 whose sequence matches the JS strain the paper used: of 28 HPIV3 F entries in UniProt it is the only one against which all 69 substitutions in the 54 variants check out, bad = 0. Seven other 539-residue entries fail on exactly one label, K141P, carrying Arg rather than Lys at 141, which is a strain polymorphism rather than a numbering error. The full-length F is used because the paper numbers in it and assays the same variants as full-length membrane-bound F in Fig. 3; the GCN4 trimerization domain and C-tag of the BLI construct are fusion partners and are not written into the sequence. Phase 7: the paper quotes fold increases over RV3 F-GCN4 for six named variants, and this file reproduces every one - S41P 5.07, N167P 6.41, L168P 3.14 and F335P 8.49 against the stated "5.1-, 6.4-, 3.1- and 8.5-fold"; T367L 2.87 against "a 3-fold increase"; and Q89M/Q222I 9.53 against "a 10-fold increase", the same 9.53 also matching G85C-L221C's stated 10-fold. Counting variants scoring above the parent gives 5 of 14 disulfides, exactly the "five out of 14 disulfides were allowed" the paper reports; the proline count comes out 10 of 19 against the paper's "nine out of 19", the extra one sitting just above the parent. Not included as separate work items: the 15 pairwise combinations of Fig. 1C, which were run on a different plate (S41P reads 0.0217-0.0292 there against 0.011-0.0208 here) and carry no RV3 F-GCN4 control row, so they cannot be rebased onto this panel, and number 15 in any case; the stem substitutions S470V and S477V and the analytical SEC thermostability of Fig. 2; the cell-cell fusion imaging of Fig. 3; and the mouse and cotton-rat immunogenicity of Fig. 7.

protein: PG-1, protegrin-1 (18-residue cationic beta-hairpin antimicrobial peptide with two disulfide bonds)
source_organism: Sus scrofa (UniProt P32194, residues 131-148, the mature protegrin-1 peptide)
readout: -PROTEOSTAT aggregation signal (relative fluorescence units) at 128 ug/ml; higher (less negative) means less self-aggregation
assay_method: PROTEOSTAT dye binding. Peptide at 128 ug/ml in PBS was mixed with PROTEOSTAT detection reagent in triplicate, incubated 10 min in the dark, and fluorescence read at excitation 530/25, emission 590/35. Triplicate readings were normalised to PBS alone and reported as the mean relative fluorescence.
remark: Sequence is the mature protegrin-1 peptide RGGRLCYCRRRFCVCVGR, taken verbatim from the source tables, which list each variant as a full 18-residue sequence rather than a mutation code; it matches UniProt P32194 residues 131-148 exactly, and mutant codes here were derived by diffing each variant against it. The orientation is inverted for readout and normalized-score, because the paper identifies self-aggregation as what drives these peptides' mammalian toxicity, so less aggregation is the better outcome. Source is Source Data sheet "Fig 3C", column "Agg (RFUs)", used as it stands; the sheet identifies peptides by ID, and sequences were joined from Supplementary Data sheet "Peptides for ML" on that ID, all 27 matching. Phase 7: regressing log10 of this file's aggregation against the haemolysis of the same 27 peptides gives R2 = 0.63, exactly the value the Fig. 3c caption states. Not included: the circular dichroism spectra of Fig. 2a-d and the haemolysis dose curves of Fig. 3b, which are spectra and curves rather than one number per variant; the 95,472 and 51,877 machine-learning predictions in Supplementary Data (predicted, not measured); and the kill curves, propidium-iodide uptake and mouse infection data of Figs. 4 and 6, which cover four variants at most.

protein: GRB2 (growth factor receptor-bound protein 2), assayed as its C-terminal SH3 domain
source_organism: Homo sapiens (UniProt P62993), expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
readout: AbundancePCA growth fitness, the log ratio of variant frequency after and before methotrexate selection, scaled so that the unmutated protein is 0; higher means more folded, soluble protein
assay_method: AbundancePCA in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The protein of interest is fused to one fragment of a split murine dihydrofolate reductase; the reconstituted enzyme confers resistance to methotrexate, so growth rate in selection medium is proportional to the intracellular concentration of the folded, soluble protein. A library of variants competes in a pooled culture for 3-5 generations and each variant's frequency before and after selection is read by sequencing; fitness is the log ratio, in triplicate.
remark: Sequence is UniProt P62993 (GRB2, 217 aa) fetched whole. Supplementary Table 4 gives each variant only as the mutated window, not the whole protein; the wild-type window occurs exactly once in the reference sequence, at residues 159-214, and mutant positions here are that offset applied. The assayed construct is not the full-length protein: it is the isolated C-terminal SH3 domain of GRB2 (UniProt annotates it as residues 156-215) fused to a dihydrofolate-reductase fragment for the protein-fragment complementation assay, and only residues 159-214 were mutated. The full-length reference is used as the sequence so that positions are canonical; residues outside the window rest on provenance alone. This dataset is library 1, all combinations of 34 single substitutions chosen to preserve both folding and binding (2^34 designed), measured by AbundancePCA. Readout is the "fitness" column of Supplementary Table 4, used as it stands; higher is already better, and the WT row is the table's own row flagged WT=TRUE. The variants are combinatorial, most carrying many substitutions at once, which is the point of the paper; multi-site genotypes are joined with ":". Phase 7: the mutant codes parsed out of the deposited windows reproduce each library's stated design exactly - library 1 uses 34 distinct single substitutions at 34 sites ("the largest set of mutations predicted to preserve both molecular phenotypes consisted of 34 single aa substitutions"), library 2 uses 4 sites with 76 = 4 x 19 distinct singles ("all possible substitutions at 4 physically interacting sites", 20^4), and libraries 3 and 4 each use exactly 15 distinct singles with genotypes up to 14 and 15 mutations deep (2^15 = 32,768 designed). Not included: the "1_lenient" rows of Supplementary Table 4, which are the same library 1 AbundancePCA experiment under a more permissive confidence filter (129,320 rows rather than 71,233) and would duplicate this dataset; the inferred folding and binding free energies of Supplementary Table 5, which are model output rather than measurement; the growthrate columns, which are the same measurement on another scale; and the shallow double-mutant ddPCA data for GRB2-SH3 and PSD95-PDZ3, which belong to an earlier publication (doi:10.1038/s41586-022-04586-4).
